item.title: Toxic, bone-crushing fish from Hell terrorizes vacation waters
item.description: The silver-cheeked toadfish carries deadly tetrodotoxin and has bone-crushing jaws that can sever fingers, prompting Greek authorities to install barriers.
item.content:encoded:
A species of puffer fish with toxic flesh and bone-crushing jaws is expanding its range throughout the Mediterranean, causing local authorities to issue warnings to tourists about the risk of bites.

Some places are even taking precautions to protect swimmers and bathers from the invasive silver-cheeked toadfish, also called harefish.

The fish reportedly entered the Mediterranean through the Suez Canal and has spread as sea temperatures have warmed. It carries tetrodotoxin, a deadly neurotoxin found primarily in its flesh and internal organs, and its powerful beak-like jaws can shred fishing gear and bite through bone.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

Experts note, however, that the fish does not routinely attack people. Bites tend to occur when people try to catch, handle or otherwise interact with them.

A 2024 study published in the peer-reviewed journal Toxics documented 198 human-health incidents involving invasive puffer fish across the eastern Mediterranean between 2004 and 2023.

There were 28 records of physical attacks, at least 144 non-lethal poisoning episodes and 27 human fatalities resulting from consumption of the fish, the study found.

"The number of recorded incidents greatly increased after 2019, especially with regard to poisonings, yet whether this is related to greater media attention, or to increased fish abundance is unclear," the researchers wrote in their study.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

The Hellenic Red Cross, Greece's national Red Cross society, issued a public advisory in June cautioning that the fish’s flesh "contains a potent neurotoxin (tetrodotoxin), which makes it extremely dangerous to eat," The Times, a U.K.-based newspaper, reported.

"Because the distribution of the toxin varies, no part of the fish is considered safe to eat," the Red Cross warned. "Although the harefish’s bite is not venomous, its extremely powerful, beak-like jaws can cause serious injuries and heavy bleeding."

According to The Associated Press, the fish has "prominent, humanlike teeth," and "its skin and organs contain a powerful neurotoxin that can cause heart failure in humans if consumed."

Tetrodotoxin causes paralysis and respiratory failure. Cardiac effects can occur in the event of severe poisoning.

Greek authorities established floating barriers beneath the Gulf of Euboea between the Greek mainland and the island of Evia to safeguard people in the water, the Guardian reported.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

"Our duty and primary concern has to be the safety of our citizens," Antonis Spanos, the vice-mayor of Evia's capital, Chalkida, told the publication. "It’s better to be safe than sorry.

"Two and a half kilometers of this net will be set up in bays around the gulf to allow for a carefree summer," he added. "Last year it was bad with the jellyfish, but, as you say in English, we’ve killed two birds with one stone. Now if there are puffers, we’ll be ready for them too."

Other municipalities along the Gulf of Euboea are also installing or planning to install floating barriers and protective nets to help keep swimmers safe, according to reports.

"Authorities say the fish have not been sighted in bathing areas at Greek island resorts," reported the AP. "But in recent weeks, the fish have wreaked havoc for fishermen off the coast of Crete and several other Greek islands, chomping through nets."

The silver-cheeked toadfish has few natural predators in the Mediterranean, so its population to grow rapidly. The Greek government announced it would pay fishermen 5.33 euros per kilogram, equivalent to about $2.75 per pound, to catch the nuisance fish.

Not all pufferfish are poisonous, but the vast majority contain a lethal neurotoxin called tetrodotoxin in their internal organs and skin. Toxicity levels vary significantly by species, and farm-raised pufferfish that never eat toxin-containing prey in the wild remain non-toxic.

item.title: Henry Winkler dishes on the 'Happy Days' guest star who had a big ego
item.description: Henry Winkler revealed which "Happy Days" guest star rubbed him the wrong way by repeatedly bragging about fan mail on the ensemble-driven set.
item.content:encoded:
Henry Winkler is sharing which former screen partner didn't leave the best impression on him.

While appearing at a recent fan expo in Tennessee, the 80-year-old actor spoke about the comradery on set of "Happy Days," explaining "on our set, there was no stardom," and how one guest star failed to mesh with the rest of the cast.

"We were an ensemble. We worked hard at making it funny every week," he said. "One guy came on as a guest star, and then he was brought back a few times, and he would mention his fan mail, and I said, ‘You don’t want to talk to me about fan mail, I got 50,000 letters a week.’"

He then explained to the actor that "we don't talk about that on the set" and that "we are all here as one."

HENRY WINKLER SAYS AMERICA DOESN'T EMBRACE OLDER GENERATION LIKE OTHER COUNTRIES DO

Despite the warning, Winkler said the actor "kept doing it," later calling the guest star "an a--back." While he didn't name names, he mentioned that the character the actor portrayed was named Eugene.

Winkler played Arthur "Fonzie" Fonzarelli on the hit sitcom throughout all of its 11 seasons, from 1974 to 1984. After getting his big break on the show, he went on to enjoy a successful career in both film and television, earning a Golden Globe nomination for "Heroes," and starring in "The Waterboy," "Holes" and "Click."

After years in the industry, Winkler is still having new experiences on set, as he recently filmed his first nude scene for the first episode of the third season of "Loot."

"Maya Rudolph is one of my favorites. She is [a] brilliant person and a lovely person. So, when she asked me to be on the first episode of the third season of 'Loot,' I didn't even ask to read the script," he explained.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

He then explained that when he went to his first costume fitting, he was shocked to find "a silk robe that went to there," he said while pointing to his upper thigh. "There was nothing else."

"And then we did it in January on the beach. And I want to say the wind came from every direction," he said. "Parts of my body, large and small. … It was so cold. I was in shock. But then I was with Maya and her wonderful cast."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

While he won two Golden Globe Awards for playing Fonzie, Winkler didn't win his first Emmy Award until 2018, when he was rewarded for his work on the hit show "Barry."

He starred on the show as Gene Cousineau, an acting coach who finds himself striking a friendship with a wanted assassin, played by Bill Hader, for four seasons.

"Be yourself, be honest about your ability, prepare so that you are not a flash in the pan," he said backstage after his win, per Variety.

"When I first started here in Hollywood … I thought of myself as a tree or sapling. I planted. I wanted to grow and be strong until I couldn’t do this anymore. And what a great tree it is."

item.title: 'Wonder Woman' star Lynda Carter stuns fans with age-defying Instagram photos of her in a bathtub
item.description: Lynda Carter, 75, stunned fans with Instagram photos from the "Super Troopers 3" set, including a playful bathtub scene that sparked age-defying praise.
item.content:encoded:
"Wonder Woman" star, Lynda Carter, shocked fans with her age-defying appearance on social media.

The 75-year-old actress stunned in a series of photos shared on Instagram on Tuesday, July 28, while promoting her latest project, "Super Troopers 3."

"@supertroopers Ride Again!!! Follow them and us (returning cast) For a fantastic road romp!!" she captioned the post. "But....wait for it...the last scene! I'm naked in a bathtub???? Oh noooo, @jaychandreskhar you promised not to show that!"

In one of the photos, Carter is all smiles as she lies outside in a bathtub, with bubbles covering her chest and an elegant updo. Behind Carter is a picturesque view of a lake and greenery, and a martini is seen on a table next to her.

'80S ICON KRISTY MCNICHOL MAKES RARE APPEARANCE 25 YEARS AFTER LEAVING HOLLYWOOD

Other photos show the "Supergirl" actress posing with her arms around her co-stars and crew members on the film in a gray robe.

"My God, is she getting younger?!😍" one fan wrote in the comments section. Another added, "Still absolutely gorgeous 😍, while a third fan chimed in adding, "Can't wait! And @reallyndacarter you look amazing!! You don't age!! ❤️🔥🔥"

When speaking to People in March 2024, Carter shared her secret to looking youthful in her 70s, telling the outlet, "People still recognize me all the time as Wonder Woman," adding that since she hasn't "cut" her face, "I probably look just myself, but older."

"And the reason I've never had any facial surgery is just because I'm afraid. It's scary, because we've all seen some bad ones," she said. "That outcome is spending time in a chair with some really good people doing your hair and makeup."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

She explained that while most "actors and celebrities always look so great when they're on the red carpet," they often look like everyday people without makeup on and when wearing regular clothes.

"If everyone did a three-hour makeover before they left the house, then they'd all look amazing," she said. "What I'm trying to say is, there's a lot of effort behind those pictures. Don't think they walk out the door looking like that!"

Carter rose to stardom with her career-defining role playing Wonder Woman in the eponymous show, from 1975 to 1979. Decades after the show went off the air, fans continue to associate Carter with the iconic character, but she says she doesn't mind.

When speaking with E! News in October 2016, Carter explained that speaking about the show has never been an issue for her.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"I love the character. I love her. I think she stands for so much…I've heard so many great stories," Carter said. "She became so much more than this show or the comic book or the movie, she became a symbol for the beauty and the strength and the loving kindness and the wisdom of women…and gay men."

item.title: Calvin Ridley recalls fast-casual Mexican meal before offseason stomach bug knocked him out
item.description: Calvin Ridley says he lost 15 pounds in 24 hours from a stomach bug he blames on Chipotle, though the chain has no link to Cyclospora cases.
item.content:encoded:
Gastrointestinal issues have been in the news a lot lately (that's not a sentence I thought I'd type when I walked across the stage to receive my college degree), and now Tennessee Titans wide receiver Calvin Ridley is talking about a nasty offseason stomach bug he dealt with.

The culprit?

Well, according to Ridley, it was a meal that he had from a certain fast-casual chain known for slinging burritos, burrito bowls, and any other permutation of protein, rice and toppings your heart desires.

STOMACH BUGS SURGING AS DOCTORS SAY CERTAIN TRAVEL ESSENTIALS COULD SAVE YOUR TRIP

On Saturday, a reporter asked him about an offseason bout with a 24-hour bug.

"Oh, yeah, I did," he said. "I've actually had that a couple of times in my life; maybe three or four times. It's not a good thing. It's like a 24-hour thing, but it really puts you down pretty good."

The Titans star revealed that he actually lost around 15 pounds in just 24 hours.

WEIGHT-LOSS JOKE TURNS SERIOUS AS 'CYCLOSPORA SKINNY' TREND FUELS HEALTH WARNINGS

That's brutal. Bugs like that are 24 hours of hell.

If someone said, "Hey, pick between a stomach bug or being fed feet first into a woodchipper," obviously, I'd pick the stomach bug, but I would briefly weigh the options.

Of course, what with all of the Cyclospora and lettuce hysteria, reporters did their job and asked an important follow-up question about whether or not Ridley's dilemma was because he had eaten lettuce.

"Chipotle," he replied.

Now, come on.

First of all, it's important to note that Chipotle has not been linked to any of the Cyclospora incidents sweeping our nation's restrooms and toilet paper aisles (weird that it's still readily available, unlike the early days of COVID, right?).

We've also reached out to the company for comment on Ridley's situation.

We don't know the source of Ridley's ailment, and it's good that he's doing better, but I'm tired of Mexican food being public enemy No. 1 anytime someone gets an upset stomach.

Whenever anyone's stomach feels a bit off-kilter, they go straight to the Mexican food. Sure, maybe it played a role, but it's unfair to just assume.

I mean, it's to the point that in many people's minds, Mexican food is practically as synonymous with gastrointestinal struggles as Tums and Febreze are.

Sure, it's not going to play as nice with the ol' pipes as some other cuisines, but we all know that going in. If you're scared or have plans, maybe eat a few saltines and play it safe.

item.title: Bill Maher breaks with the left to hammer Anthony Fauci after explosive Senate hearing
item.description: Bill Maher accused Anthony Fauci of telling "actual lies" about COVID-19 origins, saying the lab leak theory was silenced over racial politics.
item.content:encoded:
Comedian and talk show host Bill Maher railed against former National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases Director Dr. Anthony Fauci just days after he invoked his Fifth Amendment right against self-incrimination 111 times during a Senate hearing over his handling of the COVID-19 pandemic.

During Friday’s episode of HBO’s "Real Time," Maher called out Fauci for telling "actual lies" about the origins of the virus responsible for over seven million confirmed deaths worldwide following Fauci’s Senate hearing on Wednesday.

"He was caught in actual lies," Maher said, adding, "The big issue to me is the origin of this, which is very important. How did it start?"

TOP 5 MOMENTS FROM FAUCI'S HEARING: PAUL BOOTS LAWYER, MORENO ERUPTS AS CONTEMPT VOTE LOOMS

The comedian pointed to Fauci’s previous assertions that the virus originated through animal-to-human contact at a wet market in Wuhan, China.

"He was telling people up front when it first began [that] it was from the wet markets. It could not — that's a conspiracy theory — if you say it escaped from the lab," Maher said.

"And he knew better," Maher continued. "Because we have him in his diary telling us what he was saying to other scientists, who were saying, ‘No, absolutely.’"

Fox News Digital reached out to Fauci for comment.

SLACK MESSAGES RELEASED BY RAND PAUL APPEAR TO SHOW AUTHORS OF KEY COVID-19 ORIGIN PAPER HELD PRIVATE DOUBTS

Maher went on to point to the controversial theory that the virus was the result of either an accidental or intentional leak from a Chinese laboratory in the same city where the first cases originated.

He also blasted Fauci over the crux of his hearing, in which he was questioned regarding the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases’ funding of "gain-of-function" research in China.

Fox News Digital previously covered Fauci’s vehement denial that the controversial research method — which involves scientists altering the genetics of a virus to better understand and treat it — led to the samples breaking free from the Wuhan Institute of Virology.

WATCH: RAND PAUL SAYS THERE'S ONE THING AMERICANS HAVE NEVER HEARD FROM FAUCI

"I would always have said, don't do it, but it's a viable debate," Maher said, referring to the "gain-of-function" research method. "It's a reasonable debate — should we soup up something that's bad, this bacteria, to study it? Maybe if it got out it would be even worse. I think that's what did happen."

In June 2025, the World Health Organization released a report in which officials determined "the weight of available evidence … suggests zoonotic spillover … either directly from bats or through an intermediate host."

Maher then challenged the controversy surrounding the lab leak theory, which has been supported by President Donald Trump, and suggested the outcry surrounding its merit was largely due to social issues — not scientific evidence.

"We could have had that debate in a rational way," Maher said. "We didn't want to do that. Because why? Because we make everything about race. And this is one of the repercussions in this."

Maher added that the pandemic brought a racial stigma surrounding the lab leak theory, creating an unfounded taboo on the topic.

"You couldn't say it escaped from the lab, because that was the racist point of view somehow — that the entire Asian continent would have been somehow complicit in this because it escaped from the [lab]," Maher said. "It was ridiculous."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

"But that is where they went," the comedian continued. "You were racist if you said this escaped from a lab. I think we've morphed from a place where we want to obviously not be prejudiced against anybody, to where people of color can never do any wrong."

Maher’s criticism of Fauci marks a notable break from his fellow left-leaning counterparts in media, who have historically stood behind the doctor.

"Once again, Bill Maher is willing to level with the country in a way the liberal, elitist media never would," Curtis Houck, managing editor of NewsBusters at the Media Research Center, told Fox News Digital. "The press should be capable of calling balls and strikes."

"But when it comes to most things and their dear Saint Fauci, they must protect him at all costs by either explaining away his damaging diary entries or not covering them at all," he continued. "The media have made the decision to be joined at the hip with Fauci, even as his credibility has dropped off a cliff."

item.title: Trump says he 'disagrees 100%' with U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro over Reflecting Pool case
item.description: Trump publicly broke with U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro on Truth Social, calling Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool damage a case of "VANDALISM."
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump publicly broke with his top local prosecutor Saturday, insisting damage to the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool was "a pure case of VANDALISM" despite federal officials citing contractor failures as they moved to dismiss a felony case against a former U.S. Olympian.

"I disagree 100% with Jeanine Pirro, the U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia, on the Reflecting Pool," Trump wrote on Truth Social. "I don’t know what she was thinking?"

Trump's remarks came one day after Pirro's office asked a federal judge to dismiss a felony destruction of property charge against former U.S. Olympian David Hearn, who was accused of damaging the landmark after allegedly pulling up a loose section of its protective lining on June 19 despite being told by a National Park Service employee to stop.

"To me, it was a pure case of VANDALISM, that included the grass, which had a big 86 47 emblazoned in giant letters on it, and other elements of the surrounding area," Trump continued, referencing a separate vandalism incident that had occurred about a week earlier.

U.S. Park Police previously discovered the numbers "86 47" etched into the grass near the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool. The phrase has become a politically charged slogan directed at Trump. Supporters of the president, including Trump himself, have argued it amounts to a call for his assassination.

WHO IS DAVID HEARN? US OLYMPIAN WHO DENIES VANDALIZING REFLECTING POOL AFTER VIRAL ARREST

Pirro's office dropped the charges against Hearn on Friday after concluding that reports disclosed by the Department of the Interior revealed that there were many flaws with the renovation project, including that the lining appeared to begin peeling days after installation.

"Given all of this newly discovered information, it is difficult to attribute the widespread damage to the Reflecting Pool to vandalism, let alone to establish that fact beyond a reasonable doubt," the motion concluded.

Trump acknowledged there potential issues with the project but rejected the Justice Department's conclusion that construction problems were primarily responsible for the damage.

"There may have been some contractor difficulty, but the major damage was caused by VANDALS!" Trump wrote.

TRUMP ADMINISTRATION HAS LOST OR ABANDONED HUNDREDS OF LAWSUITS AGAINST ANTI-ICE PROTESTERS, MIGRANTS: REPORT

Hearn was indicted on July 2 on one count of felony destruction of property after U.S. Park Police alleged he pulled at the pool's protective coating, with authorities initially estimating the damage exceeded $1,000.

According to Pirro's office, the Department of the Interior initially provided only "barebones" reports and did not disclose documents showing the Reflecting Pool's newly installed coating had begun failing almost immediately after construction.

"Had DOI been forthcoming with the information clearly in its possession, the government would not have sought a grand jury indictment," prosecutors wrote in Friday's filing.

"It was not until after the return of the indictment, that the DOI provided additional documents to the USAO-DC indicating that damage to the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool in June 2026 was the result of flawed installation by the contractor, Atlantic Industrial Coatings ('AIC'), and the rush to complete the project prior to events associated with the America 250 celebration in the weeks surrounding Independence Day 2026," the filing continued.

The case against Hearn was dismissed without prejudice, meaning charges could be brought again in the future.

Court filings show Atlantic Industrial Coatings received a no-bid contract worth more than $14 million to install a new protective lining across the Reflecting Pool's 68,000-square-foot floor.

The project began in early May but was slowed by rain and complications with the pool's expansion joints, adding pressure to complete the work before the July Fourth festivities celebrating America's 250th anniversary.

According to prosecutors, problems surfaced almost immediately.

TRUMP SHARES NEWS OF 'CRYSTAL CLEAR' REFLECTING POOL, CALLS FOR VANDALISM SUSPECT'S ARREST

Just two days after the project was completed on June 9, a National Park Service engineer reported that sections of the new lining were already peeling.

"I stated my concern that this 'overspray' along the perimeter of the pool could lead to a 1'-2' strip that is vulnerable to peeling," the engineer wrote in a June 11 email obtained by the New York Post. "The contractor would not confirm in field if this was or wasn't a risk."

Following the dismissal request, Hearn's legal team accused the government of rushing to prosecute the case.

"The Trump administration's case against Davey Hearn should never have been brought. Its dismissal today does not erase the abuse of government power in arresting and charging a patriotic American who did nothing wrong. The government’s approach was ready, fire, aim. The administration owes Mr. Hearn an apology," attorneys Norm Eisen, Mary Dohrmann and Steve Levin said in a statement to the New York Post.

Fox News Digital has reached out to Pirro's office for comment.

item.title: Heidi Klum shows off figure during yacht trip after revealing her husband told her to 'eat more'
item.description: Heidi Klum and daughter Leni Klum stun in bikinis on a St. Barts yacht, weeks after the supermodel revealed why she refuses GLP-1 weight loss drugs.
item.content:encoded:
Heidi Klum basked in the sunshine while on vacation with family.

The 53-year-old German supermodel was photographed enjoying time with her daughter, Leni, and her daughter's boyfriend, Aris Rachevsky, on a yacht off the coast of St. Barts in the Caribbean.

In the photos, the mother-daughter duo both stun in bikinis. Klum  rocked a cream-colored string bikini, which she paired with a gray baseball cap and sunglasses, and in some photos she held up her dog as an accessory.

Leni also wore a bikini, flaunting her toned body in a strapless blue top and matching bottoms, which she paired with a white hat and sunglasses.

HEIDI KLUM DITCHES BIKINI TOP, COVERS UP WITH POTATO CHIP BAG ON BEACH VACATION

Some of the photos show Leni wearing a snorkeling mask and flippers, while in others, she is taking photos of her mom, which later appeared on Klum's Instagram.

"You Are so beautiful Heidi 😍💗🔥👑" one fan wrote in the comments section. Another added, "The girlz still got it...🔥🔥"

"Tom is lucky to have an amazing woman like Heidi," a third fan wrote.

The mother-daughter vacation came a few weeks after the "America's Got Talent" judge spoke to Us Weekly about how her husband, Tom Kaulitz, went against one of Hollywood's biggest beauty obsessions and told her to "eat more."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

She told the outlet that she is "not interested at all" in GLP-1 drugs, admitting she has gained weight over the past few years. She doesn't mind the weight gain, adding, "I think with age, we look better when we're not as skinny."

"My husband was the first one who pointed that out. He said, 'You should eat more; you would look better if you had more meat on your bones.' I was like, 'What?' This is not something you're told in the industry, ever, because you're always supposed to be skinnier than you are."

While she has no interest in trying Ozempic or any other weight-loss drug, Klum said she doesn't look down on those who choose to go that route, noting, "A lot of people have a hard time getting that jumpstart."

In the past, Klum and Leni have sparked controversy due to their decision to pose together for a lingerie campaign for the brand Intimissimi, with social media users saying, "This makes me feel uncomfortable."

In response to the criticism, Klum told People that while some are questioning her decision to engage in the campaign with her daughter, she is proud of Leni, adding, "She’s fine with me like that."

"I’ve always been very open with my body," she continued. "When I’m suntanning in the backyard, I might not have a top on. I’m European … My kids don’t know me any other way and are probably more easygoing with their bodies because of it."

item.title: Baby boomers hate 10 things about today's grocery stores
item.description: From self-checkout frustrations to digital coupons and understaffing, baby boomers have strong opinions about how modern grocery stores have changed.
item.content:encoded:
Grocery shopping has changed dramatically over the past 50 years, and not everyone is happy about it.

Baby boomers — generally defined as those born between 1946 and 1964 — are particularly frustrated by many of today's grocery-store features, according to The Takeout. Technology-driven shopping is among their biggest complaints, along with several other modern grocery-store changes.

TRADER JOE'S WORKERS SHUT DOWN LONG-RUNNING CHECKOUT LINE RUMOR: 'OVER-THE-TOP FRIENDLINESS'

When asked to choose between self‑checkout and cashier‑assisted checkout — each with equal lines — 62% of respondents to a YouGov survey aged 65-plus said they preferred cashier-assisted checkout, compared to 34% who said they like self-checkout.

Fifty percent of respondents aged 45-64 said they preferred checking out with a cashier, while 44% said they would choose self-checkout. In the 18-29-year-old demographic, meanwhile, 52% said they prefer self-checkout, while 26% said they would prefer cashier-assisted checkout.

The major hangups boomers have with self-checkout is weighting produce, the lack of human interaction and the feeling they’re doing free labor, The Takeout reported.

Cleanliness and organization are what baby boomers prioritize in grocery stores, a 2024 survey published by the Feedback Group found.

Boomers have a strong preference for supermarkets (32%), the survey found, while Walmart (28%) was their second choice for grocery shopping. Gen X shoppers preferred Walmart (28%), followed by supermarkets (25%), while Gen Z opted for Walmart (23%), Aldi (20%), dollar stores (17%) and club stores (15%). Traditional supermarkets ranked last among Gen Z shoppers, with only 11% reporting this as their go-to store.

Grocery stores carefully arrange products to encourage shoppers to spend more time in the store and buy more items.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Frequent product relocations were another common complaint in the social-media responses highlighted by The Takeout.

The share of people aged 65 and older who are tech-users grew in the last decade, a 2022 Pew Research Center poll found. Despite this trend, many baby boomers say digital-only coupons put shoppers without smartphones at a disadvantage.

Trader Joe’s is an outlier, The Takeout noted, since the grocery-store chain doesn’t offer discounts or sales.

Shopping carts offer a "tactical maneuver" for some older adults who rely on them for mobility and stability purposes and as a rest aid, according to The Takeout.

Several baby boomers reacted to a Facebook post asking about their grocery-shopping experience to say they value shopping carts with wheels that swivel easily and are easy to push.

While younger generations are more likely to shop at budget grocery stores and buy off-brand products, a sizable number of baby boomers always go for name brands.

More than one in four (26%) baby boomers "rarely or almost never consider switching from their favorite brand," a Numerator survey on consumer trends found.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

A Reddit forum featured many commenters expressing frustration with the older generation for spending more money for a comparable, generic product, The Takeout reported.

Many Americans grew accustomed to encountering out-of-stock items when the COVID-19 pandemic disrupted the supply chain. But baby boomers aren’t as accepting of the reality as others, according to social-media posts on the subject.

Many retirees live on fixed incomes and rely on sale-priced products to help stretch their grocery budgets, meaning unavailable items can have a greater financial impact on older adults.

Food retailers have faced recruitment and retention challenges in recent years, and it’s a pattern keenly felt by baby boomers.

Social-media comments summarized by The Takeout suggest many boomers associate understaffing with longer checkout lines, slower service and fewer opportunities for personal interaction with employees.

Going hand-in-hand with frustrations over self-checkout and understaffed stores, many baby boomers also dislike the growing absence of dedicated grocery baggers.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Plenty of boomers complain on social media about this modern grocery-store, expressing frustration at doing their own labor, according to The Takeout.

Millennials, those born between 1981 and 1996, comprise the generation most likely to spend money on prepared grocery meals, a U.S. Department of Agriculture survey found. Prepared meals often cost significantly more than cooking from raw ingredients because shoppers pay for the added convenience.

According to research summarized by the Institute of Food Technologists from FMI’s (originally the Food Marketing Institute) U.S. Grocery Shopper Trends report, 29% of shoppers ages 65 and older reported buying prepared foods to save time, compared with 45% of shoppers ages 15 to 24.

item.title: Fans stunned at Travis Kelce's training camp physique after nuptials to Taylor Swift
item.description: Fans poke fun at Travis Kelce's physique after videos of the Kansas City Chiefs star at training camp surface online just weeks after he married Taylor Swift.
item.content:encoded:
Travis Kelce is turning heads at the Kansas City Chiefs training camp, but not with his play.

Fans were stunned by the star tight end's physique this week after his nuptials to Taylor Swift nearly a month ago. Videos of Kelce walking onto the field surfaced online, and fans didn’t hold back in the comments.

"Is he playing (offensive line) this season?" one user quipped on X.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

Another fan said Kelce is "halfway out the door with a beer in his hand."

One fan compared Kelce’s physique to his brother, former Philadelphia Eagles star center Jason Kelce.

"Bro showed up to camp looking like he has his brothers beer belly," the user wrote.

"That’s Jason Kelce now," another user wrote with a sobbing emoji.

NFL LEGEND ROB GRONKOWSKI DETAILS TRAVIS KELCE AND TAYLOR SWIFT'S 'MAGNIFICENT' WEDDING

Another fan compared Kelce to his head coach, Andy Reid.

"Looks like he’s really locked in to try and get himself into character to take Andy Reid’s job someday," the user wrote.

Multiple fans commented that he seemed to enjoy himself at the wedding buffet. Kelce’s wedding to Swift was nearly a month ago, when they tied the knot on July 3, at Madison Square Garden in front of about 1,000 attendees.

The 11-time Pro Bowler is heading into his 14th season in the NFL. Despite the Chiefs having a down year and missing the playoffs, Kelce was still productive last season. He played in all 17 games, recording 76 catches for 851 yards and five touchdowns.

His total of 1,080 career receptions is the most among active players in the NFL. If Patrick Mahomes is able to return from his ACL injury and start Week 1, Kelce will be one of his top targets.

item.title: Assisted living sent resident to doctor's appointment after giving him 18 shots, 5 am beer: officials
item.description: State investigators claim a Minnesota assisted living facility gave a mentally ill resident 18 shots of liquor in 24 hours before a telehealth appointment.
item.content:encoded:
State investigators from Minnesota's Department of Health claimed an assisted living facility provided a mentally ill man with 18 shots of liquor in the 24 hours before a doctor's appointment.

State investigators concluded that Covered Bridge Assisted Living in Holdingford was responsible for neglect after supplying resident Don Brambrink with a substantial amount of alcohol before his doctor's appointment, affiliate FOX 9 Minneapolis reported.

Authorities were alerted when Brambrink missed his scheduled telehealth appointment after drinking too much while fishing.

IS DRINKING EVERY DAY ALCOHOLISM? EXPERTS EXPLAIN WHERE CULTURE AND ADDICTION COLLIDE

The facility's registered nurse (RN) told investigators that Brambrink was "dead to the world" after drinking while fishing, according to an investigative report from the Department of Health.

"The night before the scheduled appointment, the resident was given 2 shots of alcohol at 6:54 p.m., 2 shots at 8 p.m., and 2 shots at 9:20 p.m. The morning of the appointment, staff gave the resident 2 shots at 3:55 a.m., a beer at 5 a.m., 2 shots at 5:55 a.m., 2 shots at 8:15 a.m., 2 shots at 9:15 a.m., and 2 shots at 10:55 a.m., and 2 shots at 12:30 p.m.," the report read.

Brambrink's primary care physician, according to the report, requested he be sent to the emergency room.

HIKER'S UNEXPLAINED DEATH EXPOSES DEADLY ALCOHOL WITHDRAWAL RISK MANY DON'T RECOGNIZE

"When someone from the PCP’s office called back to request vital signs be taken, the RN reported the resident was found down on the floor and that he 'didn’t feel right.' He was transported to the emergency room shortly after," the report claimed.

Hospital staff wanted to keep Brambrink overnight to evaluate him for alcohol withdrawal, but he refused, telling them he "would rather go home and continue to drink," the report states.

Brambrink's blood alcohol level was at 0.23%, almost 3x the legal limit of 0.08%, according to the report.

'BLUE LAGOON' STAR CHRISTOPHER ATKINS SAYS ALCOHOL COST HIM ICONIC 'FOOTLOOSE' ROLE BEFORE GETTING SOBER

The assisted care resident had numerous mental health diagnoses, including psychoactive substance abuse and anxiety, according to the report.

"The resident’s assessment indicated the resident had heard voices for 40 years and was homeless prior to moving into the facility. The resident was noted to have a history of alcohol use, drank alcohol daily, and had a history of meth use," the report read.

The facility had a typed-out "alcohol plan" for Brambrink which stipulated he gets two shots per hour because he was "trying to drown out the voices," the report stated.

Covered Bridge's owner Trista Barstow defended her facility's actions in an interview with FOX 9, arguing that her facility is one of the few that will take in what she called "extreme alcoholics."

"Monitoring them and trying to help them space these things out is actually a step-up. Which, sounds insane," she admitted.

"We respectfully disagree with the cited deficiency and intend to appeal. We believe our policies, individualized care planning, and documentation reflect our commitment to resident rights, resident safety, and compliance with Minnesota assisted living regulations," she said in a statement.

"Under the Minnesota Resident Bill of Rights, competent adult residents have the right to make lawful personal choices, including whether to consume alcohol. That includes the right to make decisions we may not agree with or recommend, including excessive drinking," Barstow added. "Our responsibility is not to make those decisions for residents, but to educate them about the risks, assess their health and safety, monitor for concerns, and respond appropriately when intervention is needed.

"If a resident's condition requires medical evaluation or emergency care, we take the appropriate steps to ensure their safety, including arranging transport to the emergency department when necessary."

Fox News Digital contacted Covered Bridge and the Minnesota Department of Health for further comment.

item.title: Mamdani extends deadline for NYC homeowners to seek exemption from new pied-à-terre tax
item.description: The pied-a-terre tax sparked confusion after 900,000 properties appeared on a supplemental roll, but only 17,000 homeowners received surcharge letters.
item.content:encoded:
Mayor Zohran Mamdani has given homeowners in New York City an additional month to apply to be exempt from his new pied-à-terre tax, which went into effect on July 1.

Homeowners across the five boroughs who believe they should qualify for an exemption now have until Sept. 18 to apply for one, according to City Hall. The previous deadline was Aug. 21.

The extended deadline, city officials said, applies to anyone who received notices from the Department of Finance (DOF) with the phrase "You may be subject to..."

The pied-à-terre tax, passed by the New York State Legislature in May, imposes an annual surcharge on certain high-value New York City homes worth more than $5 million that are not the owner's primary residence.

LIBERAL PODCASTER SAYS HE WAS 'DOXED' BY MAMDANI'S 'WANTED POSTER' OF PROPERTY OWNERS

The city's finance department said the extension was necessary to give homeowners more time to prove that their home is in fact their primary residence, which would mean the tax would not apply to them.

Some homeowners were initially confused because on July 24, the city published a list of more than 900,000 properties in a "supplemental market value roll" without explaining that the vast majority of them would not be getting hit with the pied-à-terre tax.

"This roll includes, but is not limited to, those properties that may be subject to the surcharge," according to a city webpage archived on Monday.

On Thursday, the webpage was updated with the following disclaimer: "Not every property or unit listed in the roll will be subject to the surcharge. Only property owners to whom DOF sent a notification by mail are required to take further action."

PROPERTY OWNER ADVOCACY GROUPS PUSH BACK ON MAMDANI'S 'RENTAL RIPOFF REPORT,' PUBLIC DATA BASE OF LANDLORDS

On Saturday, the same webpage was updated once again, clarifying that the DOF had only sent surcharge letters to 17,000 homeowners, and that only those people should concern themselves with sending an exemption application to the city.

Fox News Digital reached out to Mamdani's office for comment.

Mamdani announced the new levy on April 15 — Tax Day — in a controversial video filmed outside Ken Griffin’s $238 million penthouse on Billionaires’ Row, singling out the hedge fund manager by name as an example of the wealthy second-home owners the tax would target.

Griffin later described the video as "creepy and weird" during a discussion at the Milken Institute Global Conference on May 6. He said he watched it three times.

Despite objections from real-estate and business leaders who warned that the tax could drive investment out of the city, state lawmakers approved it as part of the budget, which Democratic Gov. Kathy Hochul signed into law on May 28.

The tax will apply during the 2026-27 and 2027-28 property-tax years to secondary residences — including one-, two- and three-family properties — worth more than $5 million.

Individual condo units and co-op units will be taxed if they are valued at $1 million or more.

item.title: Father of slain Marine speaks out after illegal immigrant who killed son faces third deportation
item.description: Martin Martinez-Ballinas, arrested five times before the fatal motorcycle crash, now faces a third deportation after illegally reentering the U.S.
item.content:encoded:
The father of a U.S. Marine killed in a hit-and-run crash involving an illegal immigrant is speaking out after federal authorities arrested the man for a third time as he once again faces deportation.

Martin Martinez-Ballinas, 38, a Mexican national, was arrested by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) on July 22 after serving a federal prison sentence for illegally reentering the United States. He now faces his third deportation, according to federal authorities.

Federal officials said Martinez-Ballinas was convicted in connection with a 2017 crash in Maryland that killed 21-year-old U.S. Marine James Ray Walden III.

ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT WHO KILLED NASHVILLE RESTAURANT OWNER TO FACE ICE DEPORTATION AFTER PRISON

After being deported in 2020, Martinez-Ballinas was caught attempting to illegally reenter the U.S. in Texas the following year and was sentenced to 15 months in prison. ICE removed him again in October 2022 but said he later reentered the country undetected, blaming the Biden administration's border policies. Agents ultimately arrested him in Maryland in December 2023.

ICE took custody of Martinez-Ballinas after he completed his federal prison sentence in New Jersey.

Walden said Martinez-Ballinas was driving without a license or insurance when he crossed into his son's lane and struck his motorcycle head-on.

ICE URGES NORTH CAROLINA TO KEEP ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT CHARGED IN TRIPLE-FATAL HIT-AND-RUN BEHIND BARS

He said he later learned Maryland officials knew Martinez-Ballinas was in the country illegally and that he had been arrested five times between 2012 and 2017 but was released each time.

Walden remembered his son as an accomplished Marine and gifted intelligence analyst whose future was cut short.

"My son was 21 years old. He was just starting his life," Walden said Friday during an appearance on The Will Cain Show. "He was in the Marine Corps. He worked for Intel. He worked for the National Security Agency as a crypto-analyst, basically Jimmy Spide with a computer. He was extremely good at what he did. His NSA boss told me that he was one of the most gifted analysts he'd ever worked with. And they were wanting him, once he got out of the Marine Corps, to come to work for them."

HARRIS CALLS FOR ICE PROBE AFTER MAINE SHOOTING AMID RENEWED 'BORDER CZAR' CRITICISM

"And all that ended in the blink of an eye," he added.

Walden pushed back on calls by some Democratic leaders to abolish ICE.

"It's got to be one of the most insane ideas I've ever heard," he said. "I cannot believe that they're condemning our ICE agents and our DHS for actually doing their job and enforcing the laws that Congress passed."

When asked what his message was for politicians seeking to eliminate the agency, Walden said his son's death showed why immigration enforcement remains necessary.

"You're never gonna understand the pain, the hole in your soul that this brings until it happens to you," he said. "And don't think that it can't. It can happen to anyone at any time. My son was minding his own business. He'd gone for a ride after work, doing nothing wrong, and his life was taken.

"You can't predict it, but you can prevent it," he added.

Walden credited President Donald Trump for prioritizing immigration enforcement.

"I believe that he's probably going to go down as one of the greatest presidents in this country," Walden said. "He stood by what he said, he said what he was going to do and he's doing it."

item.title: No cure, no vaccine: Experts warn of rare Bourbon virus after first NY case
item.description: A Long Island patient was hospitalized after researchers confirmed the first Bourbon virus case in New York, transmitted by the common lone star tick.
item.content:encoded:
A rarely diagnosed tick-borne virus with no vaccine or specific treatment has been confirmed in New York for the first time, prompting researchers to warn that additional infections may be going undiagnosed.

The Bourbon virus, "transmitted through the common lone star tick, could soon begin to complicate diagnoses if it becomes more prevalent this summer and in coming years," Stony Brook Medicine warned in a news release reporting on a study of the virus.

Only six human cases have been reported since Bourbon virus was first identified in Bourbon County, Kansas, where the first known patient was diagnosed in 2014. That patient later died.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

The virus has been associated with at least two deaths, including the original 2014 case and another reported in 2026. Researchers believe, however, that additional infections have likely gone undiagnosed.

Symptoms of Bourbon virus include fever, fatigue, rash, headache, body aches and nausea. Because there is no commercially available diagnostic test, doctors have a difficult time identifying it.

Many healthcare providers are also unfamiliar with the virus, "thus increasing the possibility of misdiagnosis," the release said.

A team of researchers led by Stony Brook Medicine confirmed the first case of Bourbon virus in New York in a patient from Long Island who developed very severe symptoms and an eight-fold rise in antibody titers of the Bourbon virus. The patient was hospitalized.

"There are a lot of lone star ticks in New York and in the Northeast, we have dense populations, and when someone is infected with Bourbon virus symptoms they are similar to other tick-borne infections," Luis Marcos, MD, Stony Brook Medicine professor and director of the Tick-borne Disease Clinic, said in the news release.

"For these reasons, the Bourbon virus is likely more prevalent than we think in our region and other cases are likely not being diagnosed."

Marcos and his co-authors said their findings show the need for expanded surveillance and better testing to improve diagnosis and track the spread of Bourbon virus.

"Without identifying the cause of an infection, the chances of developing accurate diagnostic tests or effective treatments are minimal," he said. "That is why it is so important to first understand the true impact of the virus in high-risk areas."

According to the Centers for Disease Control (CDC), "The lone star tick is widely distributed in the Northeast, South and Midwest United States."

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

The tiny, blood-feeding, parasitic arachnid has established populations in Arkansas, Connecticut, Delaware, Georgia, Illinois, Indiana, Kentucky, Maryland, Massachusetts, Missouri, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, South Carolina, Tennessee, Virginia and West Virginia, per the CDC.

Lone star ticks are an "aggressive tick," according to the agency.

"The adult female is distinguished by a white dot or ‘lone star’ on her back. The nymph and adult females most frequently bite humans and spread disease," the CDC reports.

Despite the Bourbon virus’ severity, "only a select few [ticks] bite and transmit bacteria, viruses and parasites (pathogens) that cause diseases in people," according to the CDC.

To avoid tick bites, people should wear protective clothing, such as pants they can tuck into boots and long-sleeve shirts.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Experts also recommend applying insect repellent, such as permethrin, to clothing and outdoor gear – not directly on the skin.

Stay out of tall grass and on well-beaten trails whenever possible, as ticks thrive in overgrown and heavily wooded areas.

Check for ticks after spending time outdoors and remove them as soon as you find them. Seek medical attention if you develop fever, rash, fatigue or other flu-like symptoms in the days or weeks following a tick bite.

item.title: Saturday at the Spa: Saratoga Race Course picks for Jim Dandy Day and two other graded stakes races
item.description: Commandment tops Jim Dandy Stakes picks at Saratoga Race Course, plus best bets for the Saratoga Special and Lake George Stakes on Jim Dandy Day.
item.content:encoded:
Saratoga Race Course delivers a loaded Saturday card on Aug. 1, highlighted by three graded stakes races featuring promising juveniles, talented turf runners and some of the top three-year-olds in horse racing.

The action begins with the Grade 2 Saratoga Special Stakes, where a field of lightly raced two-year-olds will sprint 6½ furlongs on the dirt for a $250,000 purse.

Later, three-year-old fillies take center stage in the Grade 3 Lake George Stakes on the inner turf course before the Grade 2 Jim Dandy Stakes headlines the card. Here are my best bets for all three stakes races Saturday at the Spa.

OUTKICK SPORTS CARTOON OF THE DAY

6.5 furlongs on dirt for two-year-olds with a $250,000 purse.

Since the field is made up of lightly raced two-year-olds, I’m taking a shot with #5 Uncle Kef (12-1), with jockey Irad Ortiz up, who has been the top-earning jockey in several Saratoga summer meets.

NCAA ROCKED BY COLORADO JUDGE'S 2022 CLASS ELIGIBILITY RULING THAT COULD RESHAPE COLLEGE SPORTS THIS YEAR

Uncle Kef is getting 12-1 on the morning-line because this is his first race on turf. He broke his maiden on a synthetic surface on debut and finished fifth on that same surface in his only other start.

Two early speed horses and the top two betting choices post alongside Uncle Kef, so maybe he rises to the occasion, runs with his rivals and Ortiz wins this race on the closing stretch. There is a better chance of this happening than the 12-1 odds imply.

One-and-one-sixteenth miles on the inner turf course for three-year-old fillies with a $225,000 purse.

It's not a great price, admittedly, but the #8 Deeper Learning (7-2) is my favorite horse in the race. She has the best jockey (Flavien Prat) and trainer combo (Chad Brown) in the field. Prat is 2-for-3 on Deeper Learning and they won on debut on the Spa’s turf at this distance last summer.

Her 85 Beyer speed figure that day remains her career best in four races. I’m placing a few other horses under Deeper Learning in an exacta for various reasons.

The #1 Honfleur (10-1) is another Brown horse and he prints money on the Saratoga turf in the summers. #3 Candy Moonshine (15-1) has run faster in all eight races and has made the money in her three career races at this distance. Then there is #4 Time to Dream (5-1), who has the most graded stakes experience in this field and great connections.

One-and-one-eighth miles on dirt for three-year-olds with a $500,000 purse.

This is pretty much a four-horse field since the #2 Asked and Answered (30-1) is winless in six career races. I hate betting favorites, but #5 Commandment (6-5) is by far the best horse in the field and he was part of my winning trifecta ticket at the 2026 Belmont Stakes at Saratoga.

Commandment is 4-1-0 in seven career starts and 1-0 at this distance. Ultimately, 6-1 is the longest price of the other three horses in this field with a chance to win, and that’s not enough to take against Commandment, who I like.

item.title: 'Sophie Night' to strike Minnesota as WNBA firmly becomes next frontier for 'Save Women's Sports' movement
item.description: Jennifer Sey is organizing a "Sophie Night" rally outside Target Center before the Indiana Fever face the Minnesota Lynx and coach Cheryl Reeve.
item.content:encoded:
Jennifer Sey saw what happened during the Indiana Fever’s game against the Seattle Storm and insisted the "Save Women’s Sports" movement needed to follow Sophie Cunningham to Minnesota on Sunday.

"When I watched the response in Seattle, frankly, the rally was really quite positive," Sey told Fox News Digital. "My understanding from folks I know that were there, our side, those supporting Sophie and standing up for women’s sports, outnumbered their side 10 to one, which is new. That’s a real shift."

"As soon as I saw that, I felt like, ‘Well, I want to support her, too, at upcoming games.’ So I figured I’ll go to Minnesota," she added.

SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM RALLY ROCKS WNBA GAME AS 'SAVE WOMEN'S SPORTS' ACTIVISTS FACE COUNTERPROTEST

Sey, the former U.S. national gymnastics champion and founder of XX-XY Athletics, is organizing a "Sophie Night" rally outside Target Center before the Fever play the Minnesota Lynx on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET.

It will mark the third consecutive Fever road game accompanied by a rally supporting Cunningham and her recent statements about protecting women’s sports. The movement began in Seattle on Tuesday, continued in Portland on Friday and will now move into another deep-blue Democrat stronghold.

Sey expects the attention generated by the previous rallies — and the controversy that erupted inside the Seattle arena — to draw a larger and potentially more contentious crowd in Minneapolis.

"I think there will be more people there than there were in Seattle, just because now there’s been so much attention put on Seattle," Sey said. "And I think there could be more contentiousness."

"But our intent is to be, of course, very peaceful and nice," she added. "We just want to honor Sophie and thank her, because it really is meaningful in this fight."

Cunningham became a flashpoint in the national debate after saying she wanted to protect girls in locker rooms and athletic competitions from having to go against "biological men." She later called her position "common sense" and refused to back away from it.

The Minnesota rally will also bring the movement face-to-face with one of the WNBA’s most prominent supporters of transgender inclusion.

Lynx head coach and president of basketball operations Cheryl Reeve recently called political efforts to restrict transgender athletes "sort of sickening" and argued lawmakers were trying to manufacture a problem.

"Exclusion is never the answer, separate isn’t equal, and trans lives matter," Reeve said.

Sey called Reeve’s argument "ludicrous."

"There would be no WNBA if there was no such thing as women’s sports," Sey said. "A third-rate NBA player that never sees time on the court would slay in the WNBA, and we all know it."

CAITLIN CLARK KEPT FROM REPORTERS DESPITE TRIPLE-DOUBLE NIGHT AS COACH GOES VIRAL FOR WOMEN'S SPORTS COMMENTS

"This isn’t about trans. This is about males in women’s sports," she added. "Women’s sports are for women."

Sey acknowledged that the WNBA’s decision not to punish Cunningham represented progress, but she argued the league has not publicly supported the Fever guard.

"I have two minds on this because I wanna recognize the progress that's been made, um, which isn't to say enough has been made. Sophie Cunningham made a clear statement. She didn't back down. She hasn't been suspended by her team or from the league. I believe just a year ago she would've been. So that is progress. But she also hasn't been supported." Sey said.

The controversy intensified during Tuesday’s game at Climate Pledge Arena.

The WNBA later fined Keaton an undisclosed amount and barred her from Seattle’s next five home games. Storm majority owner Ginny Gilder issued a public apology, but the family of one of the girls told Fox News Digital that Keaton had not personally contacted them.

The incident became a rallying point for prominent women in the movement, including Independent Council on Women’s Sports (ICONS) co-founder Kim Jones, and ICONS ambassadors women’s fencer Stephanie Turner, former Utah State and Weber State volleyball player Kaylie Ray and University of Arkansas soccer and track athlete Ainsley Erzen.

Jones said the league’s response showed that female athletes may now be able to discuss the issue without immediately facing punishment.

"I think that the WNBA has made clear that they are going to let their athletes speak their mind when it comes to the protection of women and girls in sports," Jones told Fox News Digital. "I’m glad to see that they are not censoring or punishing their athletes for speaking up."

But Jones called that response "the bare minimum."

"I do wish that the WNBA were being more proactive about recognizing the importance of protecting the female category themselves," she said. "I wish that they would sit down at the table, listen to female athletes who have been going through this, give some credence to the IOC and recognize that these policies that have allowed male athletes entrance into the women’s sports category have been a really horrible thing for women to have to face."

Turner became a national figure in 2025 when she took a knee and refused to fence a transgender opponent at a USA Fencing-sanctioned tournament. Officials disqualified Turner and placed her on 12 months of probation, though USA Fencing later changed its eligibility rules to prohibit biological males from the women’s category.

"I’m honestly kind of surprised that Sophie hasn’t faced much backlash from the WNBA, because historically it’s been pretty hard for any woman to come forward about this sort of opinion without getting massive blowback from her organization," Turner said.

Turner said the treatment of the teenagers in Seattle disturbed her even more.

"I’m not a little upset. I’m very upset with what happened to the girls who were cheering Sophie on," she said. "I think there could’ve been maybe a little bit more protection for them offered by the WNBA."

Turner said she has faced similar hostility while wearing XX-XY merchandise in Philadelphia. She alleged people have followed and filmed her in public, including one person who trailed her through multiple train cars on SEPTA.

"Stalking is probably the biggest issue that I face," Turner said. "I have no idea where these videos are going. I don’t have social media, so it’s not like I ever really see them."

Ray said she found the WNBA’s decision to discipline Keaton encouraging but questioned how the confrontation could have occurred in the first place.

"I think it was encouraging to see the response and that the co-owner is being held accountable," Ray said. "But I do think it’s really bizarre that at a women’s professional sporting event, girls that get to go sit courtside, wear their XX-XY gear and are cheering on a particular athlete would face any type of backlash."

"The fact that comments were made at all is outrageous," she added. "Especially seeing how young those girls are, it always truly baffles me that adults — and in this case an owner, someone in a position of power — feel the need or feel obligated to tear down young women."

Ray previously competed against former San Jose State transgender volleyball player Blaire Fleming and later joined a lawsuit challenging the Mountain West Conference’s handling of the controversy.

She said she and her family were doxxed after a recent viral exchange with Arizona Democrat state Sen. Catherine Miranda during a legislative hearing.

"Myself and my family got doxxed online and had people threatening to come to our house," Ray said. "A couple accounts online posted my house, my location, told my whole story, said that I was involved in the lawsuit, and some of the comments on the posts were inciting violence."

Ray said her family filed a police report, but detectives told them they could not act without a specific threat or incident.

"There was nothing they could do about it until something happens or if there are specific actionable threats," she said. "They were like, ‘Let us know if you see anything at your house or if someone breaks in.’"

Erzen, a dual-sport Arkansas athlete and plaintiff in a lawsuit challenging the NCAA’s previous transgender eligibility policies, said Keaton’s punishment felt significant only because female athletes had received so little institutional support in the past.

"Realistically, this only feels like a win because we’ve been getting below the bare minimum for so long, and we finally are getting the bare minimum," Erzen said.

"There’s no reason teenage girls should go anywhere in a shirt that says XX-XY — no controversial messaging, just there are men and there are women and they are different — and be treated that way," she added.

Erzen said she has also received death threats and personal attacks over her advocacy.

"My personal favorite when I post or go out in public in a shirt is people telling me that I look like I’m trans or I look like a man," Erzen said. "The hypocrisy is insane."

"But I hope this is a step in the right direction, and I hope it encourages more girls to speak out," she added. "Even though they shouldn’t have had to go through that, the issue is gaining more and more traction because of it."

The movement’s expanding presence could continue beyond Minnesota. Participants in the roundtable expressed interest in future rallies in Phoenix, Philadelphia, Indianapolis and Chicago, where the Fever are scheduled to play next Saturday.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST SPORTS NEWS

For now, Sey is preparing to bring the campaign inside Target Center. She purchased two seats close to the court and secured four additional tickets to give away to rally attendees.

"We are going to come with love, as Sophie would say," Sey said. "There will be no screaming or name-calling on our part. We’re there to support Sophie and come together because we all agree that women’s sports should be protected."

"We welcome dissent," she added. "But do so peacefully, and leave us alone."

item.title: Chicago teachers union boss vows to push petitions for Mayor Brandon Johnson’s re-election
item.description: Stacy Davis Gates says she'll personally collect petition signatures for Brandon Johnson's re-election bid, praising his billion-dollar school funding.
item.content:encoded:
Chicago Teachers Union (CTU) President Stacy Davis Gates signaled firm support for Mayor Brandon Johnson’s political future, declaring in a recent interview that she is prepared to hit the pavement to collect petition signatures for his re-election bid.

"I hope to see Mayor Johnson come off the sideline and I hope to see the people who support him get out here and pass a petition. If he's not going to pass one, I'll pass one for him," Davis Gates said in an interview with WTTW News on Tuesday.

"Where the governor has failed to fund our schools, the mayor has given us a billion dollars… I don’t think we’ve done better at Chicago Public Schools than under [Johnson’s] leadership," she added. "And so I'm looking forward to that progress."

CHICAGO MAYOR MAKES STUNNING ADMISSION ABOUT ATTENDING BEARS GAME WHILE TRYING TO KEEP TEAM IN CITY

The union leader’s enthusiastic backing comes despite ongoing scrutiny surrounding Johnson's deep alignment with the CTU and growing concerns over declining academic performance across Chicago Public Schools (CPS).

In 2023, the CTU endorsed Johnson—a former public school teacher, union organizer, and CTU legislative coordinator—helping propel him past incumbent Mayor Lori Lightfoot in the primary and defeating former CPS CEO Paul Vallas in the runoff.

According to financial disclosures analyzed by the Illinois Policy Institute, the CTU funneled more than $2.6 million directly into Johnson’s 2023 campaign, while teachers unions collectively poured in over $6 million.

CHICAGO PUBLIC SCHOOLS DECLARE MAY 1 A 'DAY OF CIVIC ACTION' FOR STUDENTS

Throughout his tenure, critics have argued that Johnson’s policy agenda is dictated by his former employer. Johnson, however, has consistently dismissed allegations that he is beholden to the union machine, telling ABC 7 in 2023 that his platform represents a shared commitment to "uniting the city around a set of values that the people of Chicago obviously want."

During his first term, Johnson oversaw the transition toward a historic governance shift for CPS. Under state legislation enacted in 2021 — a long-held CTU policy objective — Chicago established a 21-member hybrid school board. Following the November 2024 elections, 10 board members were elected by voters, while Johnson appointed the remaining 11 members, including the board president. Voters will elect all 21 seats in late 2026, transitioning CPS to a fully elected board in January 2027.

The CTU’s political maneuvers come as the district battles a severe enrollment crisis paired with soaring operational costs.

During the 2024 collective bargaining negotiations, internal union documents obtained by news outlets revealed a 142-page wish list of over 700 demands. The Illinois Policy Institute estimated the total cost could exceed $50 billion.

Among the union's demands were a 9% annual wage increase through 2028, 100% coverage for abortions and fertility treatments, and $2,000 stipends per child for migrant families. Another demand was new district-wide climate and social-justice mandates, including fully electric bus fleets and dedicated "gender support coordinators" at schools.

The CTU has frequently drawn sharp public criticism for prioritizing political and social activism over core academics. Earlier this year, The Washington Post editorial board called out the union's aggressive push for social justice initiatives in a district where reading and math proficiency scores continue to hover at alarming lows.

Documents obtained by Fox News Digital earlier this year also highlighted substantial union spending on left-wing political causes and opposition to federal immigration enforcement operations.

A CTU spokesperson pointed Fox News Digital to a statement Davis Gates made during an interview with WGN9 three months ago.

Highlighting the CTU’s internal democratic process, Davis Gates dismissed doubts over the union’s continued alignment with Johnson ahead of potential endorsement discussions. Yet, she added that Johnson "will also face the political action committee of the teachers union."

FAR-LEFT ACTIVIST CONFERENCE AT TEACHERS UNION HQ RAISES CLASSROOM CONCERNS

"He knows that, as he used to help lead that committee, and he'll talk to our committee about what it has meant to be mayor–what it meant in the impact of his work, and they'll make a recommendation, and we'll take it through our House of Delegates."

item.title: Socialist Spanish PM blasts Meloni over restored border controls after Ceuta surge, demands emergency meeting
item.description: Pedro Sánchez called Europe's response "selfish" and "unlawful" after Italy suspended Schengen Area free-travel arrangements with Spain over the crisis.
item.content:encoded:
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez broadly blasted his fellow European leaders for their response to the surge of tens of thousands of migrants from Morocco to the Spanish border, seemingly criticizing Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni for deciding to resume European border controls in the wake of the incident.

Sánchez appeared to take issue with Italy's decision to temporarily suspend Schengen Area free-travel arrangements with Spain. The Schengen Area is an agreement between 29 European countries which abolishes passport controls and allows people to travel across European borders without providing documents.

"In the current international context, the European Union cannot afford this kind of selfish, polarising and unlawful reaction," Sánchez said in a letter obtained by the Agence France-Presse (AFP) news wire.

Sánchez, who leads the Spanish Socialist Workers' Party, touted his country's quick turnaround in expelling nearly all of the 50,000-60,000 migrants who crossed the border back to Morocco.

"Despite these indisputable facts," Sánchez wrote, "the reaction of European governments over the past few hours has been rather asymmetric. Most have showed us their support and solidarity, and have offered their assistance. Others, however, have chosen to attack Spain and to call for its temporary exclusion from the Schengen Area."

MIGRANT CRISIS PUSHES ITALY TO RESTORE BORDER CHECKS WITH SPAIN, TESTING EUROPE'S OPEN-BORDER SYSTEM

"Such an attitude — driven by prejudice, fake news, ignorance, or political interest — is not only contrary to European law, humanitarian law, and the principles of solidarity that bind us together," he reportedly wrote. "It is also contrary to Europe’s long-term interests and to the most basic common sense, because Ceuta is not part of the Schengen Area, because there are almost no irregular migrants left unreturned, and because Spain is, according to Frontex, one of the least porous external borders of the European Union, with a number of irregular entries that is half that recorded, for example, in Italy in recent years (2021–2026)."

Sánchez additionally requested a formal meeting of the interior ministers of all 27 European Union countries in the letter, which was addressed to European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, European Council President António Costa and Irish Prime Minister Micheál Martin.

Ireland is currently serving its one-year term as the rotating presidency of the Council of the European Union.

Sánchez's request followed a mass stampede of migrants from Morocco into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta, which shares a land border with Morocco in North Africa. Approximately 50,000-60,000 people illegally rush over the border into European territory, according to Spanish local and national authorities.

The shocking footage of the flood of people prompted a worldwide response, including from President Donald Trump.

Meloni, a conservative, announced the signing of a letter by 22 EU countries calling for stronger borders.

"The images arriving from Ceuta have once again demonstrated how urgent it is for Europe to respond to illegal immigration," Meloni wrote in a Saturday post on X.

"This is why Italy has promoted, together with Denmark, a letter signed by 22 EU member states, which calls for joint action to strengthen external borders, combat irregular immigration, fight human traffickers, make returns more effective, and eliminate any factor that could incentivize new illegal entries. It is an important signal: the line that Italy has long supported is today shared by an ever-growing number of European nation. Defending the external borders of the Union is not the interest of a single Nation. It is a shared responsibility of Europe," Meloni concluded.

Irish Justice Minister Jim O’Callaghan, as part of Ireland's EU presidency, will convene a meeting of the EU's Justice and Home Affairs Council to respond to the crisis, Martin announced in a Saturday post on X.

WHITE HOUSE BLASTS SPANISH GOVERNMENT AS THOUSANDS OF MIGRANTS SURGE FROM MOROCCO, EMERGENCY REQUEST DENIED

Ceuta's President Juan Jesús Vivas said at least 60,000 people — or about 70% of the territory's population — crossed over from Morocco. Spain's interior ministry released its own figures shortly after Vivas spoke Friday, estimating that some 50,000 people had crossed from Morocco since Thursday. It added that 48,300 had already returned to Morocco by Friday evening, with hundreds more going back by the hour.

Von der Leyen claimed none of the migrants who crossed into Ceuta made it to the European mainland and that virtually all of them had returned to Morocco.

"The good news is that the vast majority of those who arrived illegally have returned to Morocco, due to the effective work of Spanish and Moroccan law enforcement. Not a single person reached mainland Spain or the rest of the EU," she wrote in a Saturday morning post on X.

At least 67 people were killed in the border rush. As a result, Spain announced it was installing a 500-meter-long barrier in the sea to combat future migration pushes.

Fox News Digital contacted the offices of the Spanish, Italian and Irish prime ministers and the office of the European commissioner.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: DSA candidate pushes federal AI datacenter moratorium with Michigan early voting underway
item.description: DSA member Will Lawrence calls for a federal moratorium on new AI data centers, saying billionaires are abandoning democratic principles in small towns.
item.content:encoded:
Michigan House candidate and Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) member Will Lawrence advocated for a national data center moratorium Saturday during an exclusive interview with Fox News Digital.

"What I see is that there is an urgent need to have a federal moratorium on new AI data centers so that we can have a national conversation about if we're going to be generating this hyper intelligent AI, what's the best way to do it, and how do we ensure that it benefits everybody rather than just a few billionaires in Silicon Valley?" Lawrence said at a campaign event in South Lansing, Michigan.

"I do support a federal moratorium because there may be a right way to build these data centers and generate super-intelligent AI, but what's happening now is the wrong way, because it's abandoning the basic principles of democracy and self-determination that are foundational to the American identity," he also said.

BLANCHE URGED TO INVESTIGATE ALLEGED FOREIGN INFLUENCE IN FIGHT AGAINST DATA CENTERS

"You have billionaires from Silicon Valley and Wall Street who are coming into small towns and then just telling everybody, 'Trust us, trust us, your energy bills aren't going to rise. This is going to be a great deal for everybody,'" Lawrence continued.

In addition to backing a data center ban, Lawrence also bashed President Donald Trump for a number of policies and, like other DSA members, advocated for major campaign finance reform in the form of publicly funded elections.

"There's a lot of money in politics, there's no doubt about it. And, I think it does a disservice to the democratic process," Lawrence said.

SUPREME COURT STRIKES DOWN LIMIT ON PARTY CAMPAIGN SPENDING IN COORDINATION WITH CANDIDATES

He then took aim at the Supreme Court decision in Citizens United vs. Federal Election Commission, a landmark 2010 decision which ruled that political contributions should be treated as a First Amendment-protected form of free speech.

"Unless there's change in the Supreme Court, Citizens United will need to be overturned with a constitutional amendment because it's a Supreme Court decision. But beyond just ending Citizens United, which deals with the dark money in politics, I also support public financing of elections, which would mean that every single candidate who has legitimate grassroots support gets access to the same pool of public funding and the same amount of dollars to run their campaign with," he said.

Lawrence avoided a question about a broader slate of DSA policies – such as abolishing the Supreme Court, the presidency and the Senate – potentially turning off centrist voters.

HARRIS' 'NO BAD IDEA BRAINSTORM' FOR DEMS INCLUDES PACKING SCOTUS, ELIMINATING ELECTORAL COLLEGE

"That's not what we're talking about. So I can't speak to whether people are turned off by it or not. We're focused on stopping these AI data centers, stopping these wars around the world, and ensuring that everybody has health care," he responded.

Lawrence, who's backed by prominent leftists like Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., and Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., is running in the Aug. 4 Democratic primary to claim the House seat in Michigan's 7th district.

The district is currently represented by Rep. Tom Barrett, R-Mich., a first term congressman who won the seat after current Michigan Sen. Elissa Slotkin, D-Mich., vacated it to run for Senate.

Lawrence is vying with a number of other Democratic candidates to face off against Barrett in November's election, including former Obama National Security Council member and U.S. ambassador to Ukraine Bridget Brink.

Fox News Digital contacted the Barrett and Brink campaigns and the DSA for comment.

item.title: William Shatner says doctor dismissed key warning sign before stage 4 cancer diagnosis

Shatner underwent surgery to remove the tumor and later completed two years of immunotherapy.

"I was just in one of those moments where you want your daddy, you know, like you're little. You're feeling very little, and you're feeling, ‘this is really scary.’ And I called him," she said.
